paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God doesn't purge His people because He's done with them. He purges them because He wants them clean. The city had become a place where rulers loved bribes and the widow's plea never came before them (Isaiah 1:23), and God says He will "thoroughly purge your dross" (Isaiah 1:25).

Now listen to what comes AFTER the fire. God says, "I will restore your judges as at first," and then the city will be called "the City of Righteousness, the Faithful City" (Isaiah 1:26). Zion will be redeemed, and the ones who get redeemed are "her repentant ones" (Isaiah 1:27). Turning back to Him is the door, baker, and it's still open.

But the passage doesn't sugarcoat the other side. Rebels and those who forsake the LORD will perish, and the strong man and his work burn together with no one to quench the flames (Isaiah 1:28, 31). That's why it matters what you lean on, because the sacred oaks and chosen gardens couldn't hold up (Isaiah 1:29-30). I say lean on the LORD, because a cookie box that's sealed for the Supper is the only kind I want my name on!
